s1_comments:
String-based requirements/justifications are not convincing to me. They depend on the quality of textual data input by a user. The cost of inputting this data is large. More structured representations may be generated by tools. Requirements engineering has specification styles. 
Why does representation B use namespace:identifiers  instead of labels for row/property names like representation A. This is not a like for like comparison.
s2_comments: The quality of the contents of the metadata dominates over the structure, especially when it is just a list of strings.
s3_comments: The mapping file (in all scenarios) is presented in an obtuse, unreadable way with no new lines, indenting or syntax highlighting colours.
overall_preference_reason:
One is larger and more expressive than the other but it seems to be largely based on strings and so I have little confidence that what goes into them will be good/useful or easy to verify. I have concerns that creating more metadata is a higher burden on users and so while it may be interesting, the cost:value payoff is not obvious to me.
Most mapping lifecycle phases were only partially available and so it does not add much having those fields.
final_suggestions:
Focus on supporting the reuse decision easier. This means visualising or post-processing the metadata into an actionable recommendation rather than a list to read.
Ensure metadata fields are structured to enable data quality assessment/ cleaning and reasoning.
